catalog_quote: 4.1. Tone levels. Funke [1909:289] and Heine [1968:105] both state that Avatime has three tone levels, plus rising and falling contours. ... Ford [1971a:20] says, "In any utterance, no more than four distinct levels of tone are used ...." He labels the tones with the numbers 1-4, with tone 1 being the lowest. ... My data confirm that Ford is correct in requiring up to four, but no more than four, distinct levels for a description of Avatime tone. ... All native Avatime nouns (and many borrowed nominal roots as well) have a tone bearing prefix. ... With the exception of the ... singular class prefix and the BA, KU, and (L)I plural class prefixes, all of which always bear low tone, the tone of the prefix is a non-predictable feature associated with the specific noun root. Because the tones on these prefixes must be lexically specified, they are sufficient to demonstrate that Avatime has a…

audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: the deciding passage is verbatim at the stated locator in the held Schuh 1995 text (lines 1168-1243, sec. 4.1 pp. 57-58). (2) Deciding source is a dedicated 1995 phonology article in Studies in African Linguistics, open-access and held; it is the best available prosodic description short of Ford's 1971 unpublished thesis, which it builds on. (3) Two later independent primaries — van Putten 2014 (held) and Defina 2016 (fetched sources now to — both describe Avatime as having contrastive level tones with tone-only minimal pairs and contain no stress/accent section; they revise the inventory from four to three levels, which refines 'prule' wording at most but leaves kind=tonal, qv=TONAL-OR-PITCH-ACCENT untouched. (4) No instrumental or stress-specific study of Avatime was found in Glottolog's 14 descriptive refs, MPG PuRe, or UGSp

sources.citation: Defina, Rebecca. 2016. Events in language and thought: The case of serial verb constructions in Avatime. PhD dissertation, Radboud University Nijmegen (MPI Series in Psycholinguistics). 279 pp.
sources.quote: 'Avatime has three contrastive level tones: extra-high (marked á), high (unmarked), and low (marked à)... Some minimal pairs distinguished only by tone can be seen in (1)... Previous work on Avatime has identified four level tones: low, mid, high, and extra-high (Ford 1971a; Schuh 1995a)... Therefore, the present analysis includes only three level tones.' No word-stress or accent section anywhere in the sketch; 'accent' tokens elsewhere refer to pitch accents in the gesture/intonation literature, not Avatime word prosody.
